claim: For the canonical Sprott B flow \(\dot x=yz,\ \dot y=x-y,\ \dot z=1-xy\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\int xy\,d\mu=\int y^2\,d\mu=1\) and \(\int y^2z\,d\mu=-\int (x-y)^2\,d\mu\le 0\). Equality in the last identity holds exactly for convex mixtures of the equilibria \((1,1,0)\) and \((-1,-1,0)\). Consequently every other compact invariant probability measure gives positive mass to each of \(\{|y|<1\}\), \(\{|y|>1\}\), and \(\{z<0\}\); in particular every nonconstant periodic orbit crosses both sides of the equilibrium amplitude \(|y|=1\) and enters negative height.
integrity: All mathematical conclusions follow from exact Lie-derivative identities and invariance; no numerical trajectory, finite enumeration, or asymptotic approximation is used. Equality rigidity is checked by invariance of the support under the actual vector field.
limitations: The theorem is for compactly supported invariant probability measures of the canonical unforced Sprott B flow. It does not establish existence, uniqueness, ergodicity, or physicality of any chaotic invariant measure. The 2015 generalized-Sprott-B article was inspected only through its accessible abstract.
title: Exact stationary RMS locking and negative-height defect in canonical Sprott B
